Ten comments

From an old collection of New England fiddle music

↳ Posted by fidicen on November 21st, 2002.

1983, first edition ~ “New England Fiddler’s Repertoire”

Randy Miller & Jack Perron, 1983 / 2nd edition 2003

Page 52: “ Portland Fancy”

https://www.fiddlecasebooks.com
https://www.fiddlecasebooks.com/store/c2/Books.html
https://www.fiddlecasebooks.com/store/p1/New_England_Fiddler’s_Repertoire.html

“168 classic traditional contra dance melodies, from Batchelder’s Reel to Money Musk to Portland Fancy and beyond -- the standard contra tunes in one source. The second edition of NEFR is produced with assistance from the Gadd/Merrill Fund of the Country Dance and Song Society. Edited by Robert Bley-Vroman and Randy Miller; introduction by Newt Tolman.”

~ also from the work of New England fiddler & pianist Randy Miller:
“Irish Traditional Fiddle Music”

X: 6 “Gigue Des Sucres” - composed by Joseph Allard

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Allard_(fiddler)
See earle’s Youtube link above…that transcription minus chords…
Recording - Joseph Allard: Gigue des sucres
Record label: Victor 263932-b (78 rpm), 1934
From the collection: Folklore Quebecois Musique
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcsXvA0r4Q4v6kUQcBh7Nzg

I have a slew of Allard’s recordings and I think even a few publications. I’ll have to go searching to see if there’s anything else to add…

I heard this by Howie MacDonald on “traditonal music from cape breton island” (nimbus records 1993) where it was called “Portland Fancy”. The key chosen for that set was A major, which is impossible to find online, so here’s a transcription
